page: Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-800s-amd is an AMD EPYC-powered instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores with hyper-threading) running at 2.0 GHz. The system features 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio that aligns it with memory-optimized workloads. Storage is provided via a bundled 800 GB NVMe SSD, and the network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The x86_64 CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration such as AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing placing in the top 10% and Geekbench single-core scores in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling in the middle 50%. Memory performance is characterized by strong write bandwidth for large blocks (top 25%) and average read bandwidth across small and large blocks. Single-threaded operations like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform strongly, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput are relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive tasks that do not require massive multi-core scaling, offering a high memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside dedicated CPU resources and substantial local NVMe storage. It is well-suited for in-memory caching, text processing, and moderate database operations, though its lower multi-threaded decompression and static web serving throughput suggest it is less optimal for high-concurrency web serving or heavy multi-threaded parallel processing.
description: Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-800s-amd is an AMD EPYC-based virtual server from the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores, 2 threads per core) clocked at 2.0 GHz, 32.0 GB of RAM, and an 800 GB NVMe SSD. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it supports AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration. Performance benchmarks show top-tier single-core CPU capabilities and strong memory write bandwidth, though multi-core scaling and static web serving throughput remain average to weak. With an 8.0 GB RAM-per-core ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance offers a balanced, memory-dense profile without the cost of higher-core configurations. It is best suited for memory-intensive applications, text processing, in-memory caching, and moderate database workloads.
